# Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center (Karachi Hijama)

> Sunnah hijama (wet and dry cupping therapy), Unani (Tibb) herbal medicine, homoeopathy and Reiki at a clinic in Model Colony, Karachi, Pakistan, plus hijama home service across Karachi and online consultations for patients abroad. Booking is by WhatsApp or phone.

## Key facts

- Name: Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center
- Address: 20/32-33 Sardar Muhammad Ali Road, Nishterabad, Model Colony, Karachi 75100, Sindh, Pakistan (map: https://maps.app.goo.gl/VTyGuWixhJyLerCS6; coordinates 24.9072588, 67.1925137)
- Phone / WhatsApp: +92 322 2905560 (a second number, +92 311 3023173, is also listed on the clinic's Google profile)
- Hours: open daily, 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM
- Practitioner: Dr Misbah Shaheen Cheena (Hakeem), lead physician. The site states Dr Misbah is registered with the National Council for Homeopathy, the National Council for Tibb (Unani) and the Sindh Healthcare Commission, with certificates on display at the clinic. A qualified female practitioner is available for women patients on request.
- Serving Karachi since 1987 (the clinic's Google Business Profile also says "Established in 1987").
- Languages: English and Urdu
- Hygiene: new single-use cups and blades for every session.
- How to book: WhatsApp or call +92 322 2905560, or the booking form on the homepage (it opens a pre-filled WhatsApp message).

- Home full-body hijama anywhere in Karachi: Rs 6,500 (each extra family member +Rs 3,000)
- Online consultation: Rs 1,500 in Pakistan; USD 35 / GBP 28 / AED 130 from abroad
- Reiki: Rs 3,000 per session, Rs 7,500 for 3 sessions; distance Reiki USD 30
- New patients: 10% off the first session. Extra cups beyond a package: Rs 250 each.

## Safety (who should not have wet cupping)

Wet cupping is not done during pregnancy. People on blood thinners or with a bleeding disorder, severe anaemia, an active infection or an acutely inflamed joint are advised against it or referred to a doctor first. Patients are asked about medicines and conditions before any session. Hijama, Unani, homoeopathy and Reiki are offered as traditional, complementary care; they are not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment by a doctor, and evidence for many uses is limited.
